title: Policy engine: emit resolved autoscaling bounds + cooldown defaults; add deterministic golden tests
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: Dedicated autoscaling is adding customer-configured min/max bounds + cooldown/rate-limit knobs. The autoscaler must receive a fully resolved, validated, and versioned view of the policy config (including defaults) so that it can clamp desired replicas deterministically and provide an audit trail. This PR extends the policy engine evaluation output to include resolved min_replicas/max_replicas (and effective cooldown defaults) and adds golden tests to ensure evaluation is deterministic across runs. What changed: (1) Added an EvaluatedAutoscalingBounds object to the evaluated policy payload returned by policy-engine (includes: min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_up_cooldown_seconds, scale_down_cooldown_seconds, max_scale_up_step, max_scale_down_step, burst_to_max_enabled, and a computed enforcement_mode derived from ADR-0142 semantics). (2) Implemented defaulting in policy evaluation (not in autoscaler): when cooldowns/rate-limits are omitted, we fill with policy defaults based on hardware_class + region constraints and annotate a defaults_source field for auditability. (3) Normalized evaluation output for determinism (stable map ordering, canonical JSON marshaling, and explicit rounding where we previously had float-derived seconds). (4) Added golden tests for representative DedicatedPool configs (single-region, multi-region, migration/backfilled fields) and verified stable snapshots across 100 randomized iteration runs to catch nondeterminism. Why policy-engine (vs autoscaler) for defaults: we need one source of truth across control-plane + fleet, and we need to surface the effective values to Console (Scaling History “why did we scale?”) without re-deriving. Notes: This PR assumes schema fields landed in PR-21873; it does not change persistence. The autoscaler will start consuming the evaluated bounds output in ENG-2843. Risk: low; evaluation output is additive and version-gated (v2).
commits: policy-engine: add EvaluatedAutoscalingBounds to evaluated policy payload
policy-engine: implement cooldown/rate-limit defaulting for Dedicated autoscaling bounds
policy-engine: canonicalize evaluation output (stable ordering + duration normalization)
tests: add golden fixtures for evaluated autoscaling bounds and determinism stress test
docs: update policy evaluation schema docs + examples
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we be explicit about whether max_replicas is a hard cap in evaluation output? I want autoscaler to be able to treat this as a clamp without second-guessing semantics.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep. I added enforcement_mode=HARD_MAX and a short comment referencing ADR-0142. Also included a defaults_source field so we can explain whether values came from customer config vs policy defaults.

Benji Okafor (review): Golden tests look good, but I’m nervous about long-term churn. What’s the rule for updating goldens when we add a new field? Also, can we ensure goldens aren’t sensitive to map ordering?

Jordan Lee (author): The serializer now uses canonical JSON (stable sort keys). For goldens: adding a field will fail the tests; update via `./scripts/update_goldens.sh` in the same commit where we change schema. I added a README blurb in tests/ about expectations.
Allison Grant (review): Please confirm we’re not emitting pool_id / customer identifiers in the evaluated payload that might get mirrored into decision logs with high-cardinality labels later.

Jordan Lee (author): Confirmed. EvaluatedAutoscalingBounds includes only config values + defaults_source + enforcement_mode. No identifiers beyond what’s already in the envelope. Also added a note in policy-eval-output.md about avoiding identifiers in nested evaluated blocks.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Default cooldowns based on hardware_class: are these aligned with fleet team recommendations? For H100 vs A10 we’ve seen oscillation differences.

Jordan Lee (author): Pulled initial defaults from the fleet oscillation analysis doc (A10 slightly longer scale-down cooldown). I kept the mapping centralized in autoscaling_defaults.go so we can tune without touching evaluation logic. Happy to adjust numbers if you want different baseline before dogfood.
Sean Gallagher (review): Determinism test: can we make sure it runs in CI without flaking/timeouts? 100 iterations might be heavy.
Jordan Lee (author): Good call. Reduced to 25 iterations in normal CI with a `STRESS_DETERMINISM=1` flag for 200 iterations in nightly. Also added a 2s timeout per test to avoid hangs.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM after the determinism iteration tweak. Thanks for keeping defaults in policy-engine; this will make Console/audit much easier.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Please follow up with ENG-2846 to ensure decision log metrics do not label these raw values (use events/logs not labels).
Jordan Lee (author): Merging (squash) once Buildkite finishes schema-compat rerun.
release_notes: Policy evaluation output now includes resolved autoscaling bounds + cooldown defaults for Dedicated pools (v2 evaluated payload).
Added golden tests + determinism checks to prevent nondeterministic evaluated config output.
